title: Security posture discovery with Aventis Systems
summary: Initial security posture discovery for potential Redwood deployment. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PII-sensitive workloads. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO compliance, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS, data residency, and model caching/logging. AE/SE explained deployment tradeoffs and next steps: share SOC2 report, architecture diagram for private deployment, schedule technical deep dive and benchmark
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Alex to share SOC 2 Type II report and security whitepaper (link) by 2026-03-25
Priya to schedule technical deep dive and demo of Private deployment (week of 2026-03-30)
Customer to provide compliance checklist and any specific encryption KMS provider (by 2026-03-27)
Redwood to propose pilot configuration and pricing for Dedicated capacity
action_items: Alex Morgan - send SOC2 report + security whitepaper by 2026-03-25
Priya Shah - schedule technical deep dive + invite infra team by 2026-03-30
Jordan Lee - share Aventis compliance checklist and required regs by 2026-03-27
Maya Chen - provide list of preferred KMS/HSM vendors and VPC requirements by 2026-03-27
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood. we got Priya on from engineering too. hows it going?
[00:06] Jordan: hey alex, thanks. Jordan here, ciso at aventis, we also have Maya and luis. just to set context we run PII and PHI in some products so security is top priority.
[00:15] Alex: totally understood. goal for today is a security posture discovery - SOC2, iso, sso, rbac, audit logs, encryption and data residency. and to lay out hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.
[00:28] Priya: quick hi from me. i'll cover technical bits like network isolation, k v cache and logging.
[00:33] Maya: great. first question, are you SOC2 type II compliant today?
[00:38] Alex: yes we are SOC 2 type II, we also have an ISO 27001 roadmap, we can send the report. i'll drop the SOC2 report after.
[00:45] Jordan: perfect can you confirm scope, e g does it cover private deployments and dedicated infra or only hosted?
[00:52] Alex: good q. the SOC2 report covers Redwood hosted control plane and the hosted inference offering, dedicated pools and private deployments have overlapping controls; for private we provide the control plane configuration and docs, but the customer-managed infra portions are outside our audited scope typically - we'll call that out in the report.
[01:10] Luis: ok legal will need the delineation of responsibilities. also need proof of encryption at rest and in transit plus key management.
[01:18] Priya: for encryption: all traffic to hosted api is TLS1.2/1.3, data at rest in hosted is encrypted with customer keys available via KMS integrations. we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS today, HSM options on request. for private, keys can live in your KMS.
[01:36] Maya: are logs and payloads retained? where do model prompts end up? we have strict retention rules.
[01:42] Alex: by default hosted offers configurable logging/retention; we have opt-in request logging for hosted, and by default we don't persist prompts longer than 30 days unless trace/debug is enabled. for dedicated/private we can enforce retention 0-90 days or integrate with your S3 log sink. we'll need to map to your retention policy.
[02:03] Jordan: do you persist kv cache or prefixes for performance? could that leak PII?
[02:09] Priya: good callout. the KV cache is in-memory for serving and can be configured not to persist between sessions. when caching is enabled we can mask or strip user identifiers before caching; we also have options to disable prefix caching for sensitive endpoints.
[02:26] Maya: what about RBAC and SSO? we use SAML and Okta.
[02:30] Alex: we support SSO via SAML and OIDC; full SAML integration with Okta is common. RBAC: role-level controls in the console, API keys are scoped to projects and roles, and we integrate with SCIM for provisioning.
[02:45] Jordan: audit logs - do you provide detailed logs for token-level transactions and admin actions? retention and export?
[02:51] Priya: yes audit logs for admin events, token creation, model rollouts, and route changes. for hosted we can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or push to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket. retention configurable; by default 90 days for admin audit and 30 days for request traces unless extended with an add-on.
[03:14] Luis: legal will want to see sample logs to validate PII redaction.
[03:18] Alex: we can share redacted samples and our logging schema.
[03:22] Jordan: regulatory - any experience with HIPAA or healthcare regs?
[03:26] Priya: several customers in healthcare use our dedicated or private deployments; we provide a HIPAA addendum and support BAAs for private deployments when deployed in customer-controlled infrastructure. hosted is possible in controlled conditions but typically customers choose dedicated/private for PHI.
[03:45] Maya: ok network segmentation - for dedicated pools can we have VPC peering and strict egress rules?
[03:51] Priya: yes, dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed NAT/egress. private deployment gives you full network control; dedicated is isolated at infra layer with tenant controls and egress restrictions.
[04:06] Jordan: model provenance - do you store model artifacts or are models ephemeral? we need to know what versioning and reproducibility guarantees you provide.
[04:14] Alex: we keep model artifacts in versioned registries. for hosted we manage the storage; you can pin versions and we provide audit trails for model rollouts. for private you host artifacts yourself or we can push images to your registry.
[04:31] Maya: about penetration testing - do you run pentests and can customers perform pentests against dedicated/private?
[04:37] Priya: Redwood performs annual 3rd-party pen tests; we can share a summary. customers can run pentests in private/dedicated environments with a review and scoping. hosted customer-initiated pentests are supported but need coordination and a contract clause.
[04:55] Jordan: SLA and uptime - what's typical for dedicated?
[04:59] Alex: dedicated has SLA-backed uptime targets and latency SLOs; we'll include specifics in the offering. for mission-critical we recommend dedicated or private.
[05:10] Luis: data residency - Aventis has EU residency requirements for certain products. can you guarantee region-specific hosting?
[05:16] Alex: yes hosted supports region selection for data residency; dedicated can be provisioned in a specific region, and private obviously stays in-region. we'll flag any cross-region fallbacks and provide a contract clause.
[05:31] Maya: keys lifecycle management - rotate keys, cloud KMS integration, and who can see keys?
[05:36] Priya: keys are customer-controlled when using customer KMS, rotation policies supported, and Redwood never has plaintext access to customer-managed keys. for hosted we support envelope encryption with customer KMS to limit key exposure.
[05:52] Jordan: what about model output logging - we need to prevent sensitive outputs from being stored in logs.
[05:58] Priya: we can disable request/response logging, or route logs to customer-managed sinks with masking. we also offer a built-in PII detection pipeline to redact detected entities before storage.
[06:14] Alex: quick note on cost/latency tradeoffs: caching and batching reduce cost but increase scope for data persistence; for sensitive workloads customers often accept higher cost for stricter isolation and no caching.
[06:29] Maya: understood. what's the onboarding timeline if we choose dedicated?
[06:33] Alex: typical dedicated onboarding is 6-8 weeks for standard configs; private longer depending on on-prem. pilot options exist for a 2-4 week POC to validate controls.
[06:44] Jordan: we need to see the SOC2 report, encryption details, sample audit logs, and a contract redline.
[06:50] Alex: we'll send SOC2 and security whitepaper and sample logs. Priya will set up a technical deep dive.
[06:58] Luis: one more legal question - data deletion requests: can you confirm deletion flows and proof of deletion?
[07:04] Priya: yes we have documented deletion APIs and retention automation; for private you control deletion; for hosted we can provide attestations and logs showing deletion operations.
[07:15] Jordan: ok that helps. any recommended architecture for our use case? we run a mix of low-latency chat and batch embedding jobs.
[07:23] Priya: recommend Dedicated for chat (predictable latency and isolated pools) and hosted or dedicated for embeddings depending on throughput; we can propose a hybrid with routing rules to keep PHI traffic on dedicated/private paths.
[07:39] Maya: what about personnel security? background checks, access policies?
[07:44] Alex: we have employee background checks for ops, role-based access, and internal auditing controls; details in the security questionnaire packet we'll send.
[07:56] Luis: competitor question - some teams push for open-source self-host to control everything, how do you compare?
[08:02] Alex: self-host gives control but requires significant ops; Redwood aims to reduce ops burden while giving controls like private deployment and customer-managed keys to address that gap.
[08:17] Jordan: ok next steps recap?
[08:20] Alex: i'll send SOC2 and whitepaper; Priya will schedule tech deep dive; Aventis will share compliance checklist and KMS vendor preference; Redwood to propose pilot and pricing for dedicated.
[08:32] Maya: timeline: we'll review docs this week and aim to have a decision framework by mid April.
[08:38] Alex: perfect thanks everyone.
[08:41] Jordan: thanks, bye.
notes: Call included AE+SE from Redwood; customer focused on healthcare-like PII constraints. Discussion covered typical enterprise security topics and concrete next steps to share artifacts and schedule deeper technical review.
